newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian president in second round of PM talks.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian president in second round of PM talks.

text.p: Slovenian president Milan Kucan started a second round of talks on Tuesday with party leaders aimed at selecting a prime minister for the new government, his spokeswoman Spela Furlan said.
Furlan said talks with seven parliamentary parties would finish on Wednesday afternoon.
"If necessary the president may decide to hold another round of talks...but he undoubtedly wants to name a candidate as soon as possible," Furlan told Reuters.

Analysts said Kucan may have a hard time finding a candidate who would command majority support in a parliament divided between current Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek of the centre-left Liberal Democrats and Marjan Podobnik, head of the conservative People's Party.
The Liberal Democrats emerged as the strongest single party in the country's second general election held on November 10, gaining 25 out of 90 parliamentary seats.
The People's Party is the biggest of three rightist parties in an alliance called the "Slovenian Spring", which together won 45 seats, missing an absolute majority by just one seat.
"I believe Drnovsek is most likely to get a mandate though he may not be elected in the first round," said Drago Zajc, professor of politics at Ljubljana University's Faculty of Social Sciences.
Under the constitution Kucan must name a candidate by January 3. Parliament has to elect a prime minister with an absolute majority within two attempts.
If both votes are unsuccessful parliament can decide to vote for a third time and reach a simple majority decision. If all three attempts fail the president can call early elections.
"Eventually the parties will come to an agreement because none of them is in favour of premature elections," Zajc said.
